title: Tamper-Evident Audit Ledger + Approval Workflow (PRD sketch)
summary: Sketch PRD for an append-only, tamper-evident audit ledger and approval workflow tailored for Private deployments (customer-managed networks). Focus: enable customers and auditors to verify change approvals and runtime inference events with cryptographic evidence while supporting operator workflows and emergency rollback.
problem_statement: Customers running Redwood Private need a trustworthy, auditable record of network changes, operator approvals, and key runtime events (model rollouts, config changes, capacity adjustments). Current logs are rich but mutable and fragmented across control plane, operator consoles, and customer syslogs. Auditors ask for immutable evidence and an operational workflow that minimizes friction for routine changes while providing strong guarantees under incident conditions.
goals: 1) Produce an append-only ledger that cryptographically links entries (hash-chain) and supports optional customer-managed signing keys (KMS/HSM). 2) Define an approval gate DSL and UI that records decisions, attestation payloads, and time-based escalation. 3) Capture runtime inference-relevant metadata (model id, variant, sequence length buckets, KV-cache state reference, response-hash) tied to audit entries. 4) Offer exportable, machine-verifiable bundles for auditors and legal holds.
non_goals: 1) Not building a full blockchain or public immutable store. 2) Not replacing existing customer SIEM pipelines; provide hooks and exports instead. 3) Not designing a customer-facing PKI onboarding flow (we will integrate with existing KMS/HSM connectors).
success_metrics: - Customer audit requests satisfied in <2 business days with full verifiable evidence. - Reduction in manual evidence-gathering time by 60% for CS/Support during network handovers. - At least three enterprise pilots for ledger+approval in 90 days. - Detectable tamper alerts with false positive rate <2% in pilot environments.
stakeholders: Product (private deploy), Eng: private-deploy + infra + serving-runtime, SRE, Security & Compliance, Solutions Engineering (customer onboarding), Legal/Trust
user_personas: - Customer Network Operator: needs approvals and evidence for VPC changes. - Security Auditor: needs immutable export and verification. - Redwood Oncall/Operator: needs fast emergency approval/rollback with clear attestations. - Platform Engineer: needs API for ingesting events into the ledger.
requirements: - Ledger entries must be append-only and include entry metadata: timestamp, author (operator id or customer identity), change type, diff reference, base-hash, entry-hash, previous-hash. - Support customer-managed signing: ability to sign entries with a customer KMS key (optional). - Approval gate DSL: rules for required approvers, timeouts, auto-escalation, and fallback policies. - Evidence bundles: exportable ZIP containing entries, raw logs (redacted per policy), and verification manifest. - Retention controls: per-customer retention policy with legal-hold override. - Hooks: webhooks and SIEM syslog export for every signed entry. - UI: compact timeline view for approvals + tamper alerts; deep view for diff and raw evidence. - Runtime binding: attach inference-event references (response-hash, truncated tokens, model-version, route-id) to ledger entries when change affects serving pipelines.
user_stories: - As a Customer Network Operator, I want to request a gateway rule change and have the system route it to required approvers with a clear audit trail. - As an Auditor, I want to receive a signed evidence bundle that I can verify independently using the ledger manifest. - As a Redwood Operator, I want to mark an emergency change with a higher-attestation flow that automatically records justification and a rollback token. - As a Platform Engineer, I want an SDK to write structured audit events from internal services to the ledger.
design_notes: - Ledger storage: primary copy in control plane DB with hash-chain metadata; optional periodic anchoring (customer opt-in) to customer-managed object store or third-party anchor (S3 + signed manifest) for extra certainty. - Cryptography: support RSA/ECDSA signing via KMS connectors (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and local HSM for on-prem. - Entry format: flat JSON line per entry; publicly verifiable manifest file with entry-hashes. - Approval flow: staged states (requested -> pending -> approved | rejected | escalated -> applied). Each transition is a ledger entry with signer and attestation string. - Emergency flow: allow immediate apply with 'operator-emergency' tag; requires post-hoc review window and automated notifications. - Forensic snapshots: when requested, bundle control-plane state, model-config blobs, and minimal tokenized traces (privacy-safe) into the evidence bundle.
api_contract_notes: - POST /ledger/entries -> create entry (returns entry-id and entry-hash). - POST /ledger/entries/{id}/sign -> attach operator/customer signature. - GET /ledger/entries?range=... -> paginated read (exportable). - POST /approvals/request -> create approval request with required approvers list. - POST /approvals/{id}/action -> approve|reject|escalate with attestation. - All endpoints support webhooks for 'signed_entry' and 'approval_action' events. (Detailed OpenAPI to follow.)
operational_considerations: - Scale: expect ~5000 ledger entries/day per large customer during migration; design for bursty write patterns during rollouts. - Backups: daily snapshots + continuous replication to customer-designated region. - Monitoring: metrics for unsigned entries aging > SLA, signature verification failures, and ledger divergence. - Cost: storage delta expected ~10–50GB/month per large customer depending on retention; plan pricing add-on.
security_considerations: - Protect signing keys: if customer-managed KMS not used, Redwood must enforce HSM-backed keys for high-assurance accounts. - Limit visibility: redact sensitive payloads (PII or customer secrets) before including in public evidence unless explicitly requested. - Rate-limit ledger writes to prevent spamming attacks and ensure ordering guarantees. - Provide a 'verify' utility that validates chain integrity and signatures without exposing private data.
retention_and_compliance: - Default retention 7 years for enterprise accounts (configurable by customer). - Support legal-hold flag that freezes retention policy for specified timeline. - Provide export formats acceptable to typical auditors (CSV manifest, JSONL entries, signed ZIP). - Map retention/exports to regional data residency controls (EU/US/APAC).
ui_sketch_notes: - Timeline: compact cards (time, actor, action, status) with color-coded approval state. - Evidence drawer: side panel showing raw entry JSON, signed digest, and download evidence bundle. - Tamper alert banner: visible when chain verification fails or when entries are missing/unanchored. - Approval composer: pre-filled templates for common changes (model pin, network rule, capacity bump) to reduce friction.
open_questions: - Do we require ledger anchoring by default for Dedicated customers or opt-in? - How to handle multi-region signing when customer uses multiple KMS regions? - What is the legal acceptability of our signed evidence in different jurisdictions (work with Legal). - How to balance privacy and auditability for inference traces tied to ledger entries?
implementation_plan: MVP (Q2 pilot): - Build entry API + minimal hash-chain metadata + basic UI timeline. - Implement approval request flow with simple approver lists and webhooks. - Integrate AWS/GCP KMS for signing (customer opt-in). - Evidence bundle export. Pilot with 2 customers. Phase 2: HSM integrations, anchoring, retention legal-hold, forensic snapshot tooling, expanded SIEM connectors.
rollout_plan: - Alpha: internal Redwood ops only. - Pilot: 2 enterprise customers (Solutions Eng supported). - Beta: opt-in for Dedicated customers. - GA: configurable for all Private deployments with pricing note.
next_steps: 1) Align with Legal on evidence formats and jurisdictional constraints. 2) Engineering spike: prototype signing + verification utility. 3) Run tabletop incident with Security and a pilot customer to validate emergency flows. 4) Draft OpenAPI spec and minimal SDK example for platform engineers.
notes_to_self: Fragmented thoughts below — keep when iterating: thinking about chunked evidence bundles, delta-only snapshots to save space, and a 'consent' checkbox for customers to include redacted response hashes in exported artifacts. Also consider a lightweight attest-as-a-service for partners.
